newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan starts grain harvest, sees 1.2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan starts grain harvest, sees 1.2 mln T.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Turkmenistan has started its grain harvest, which it has forecast at 1.2 million tonnes, an official from the Agriculture and Food Ministry said on Monday.
"This volume is sufficient to cover Turkmenistan's grain consumption and implement the programme of self-sufficiency in grain proclaimed by President Saparmurat Niyazov," the official told Reuters.
The area sown to grains this year was reduced to 400,000 hectares from 600,000 last year. The Agriculture Ministry has said it expects better yields this year but gave no concrete data.
Niyazov last year sacked his agriculture minister and the heads of two regions after a disastrous grain harvest of 480,000 tonnes. The official target was 1.2 million.
"For a new failure, today's leaders responsible for harvests of grain and cotton will pay with their posts," Niyazov told an enlarged session of the state council last Monday.
The Central Asian state, facing acute bread shortages, last year spent a total of $800 million on grain imports, some from the West, the official Turkmen Press news agency has said.
